root_cause.text: The `folio_unmap_pte_batch()` function used `folio_pte_batch()` which ignored per-PTE writable and soft-dirty bits, causing restoration of lazyfree folio PTEs to incorrectly upgrade non-writable PTEs to writable, violating CoW semantics and triggering the page_table_check BUG.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "If the batch has a mix of writable and non-writable bits, we may end up setting the entire batch writable. Fix this by respecting writable bit during batching." The patch changes from `folio_pte_batch(folio, pvmw->pte, pte, max_nr)` to `folio_pte_batch_flags(folio, vma, pvmw->pte, &pte, max_nr, FPB_RESPECT_WRITE | FPB_RESPECT_SOFT_DIRTY)`, explicitly adding flags to preserve the writable and soft-dirty bits. The reproducer and crash trace confirm the BUG triggered due to a writable anonymous page being mapped into more than one process.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use folio_pte_batch_flags with FPB_RESPECT_WRITE and FPB_RESPECT_SOFT_DIRTY to avoid upgrading write permissions and losing soft-dirty bits when restoring PTEs after a failed unmap.
intent_record.what: Replaced folio_pte_batch() with folio_pte_batch_flags(), adding vma parameter, pointer to pte, and flags FPB_RESPECT_WRITE and FPB_RESPECT_SOFT_DIRTY. Added explanatory comment.
intent_record.how: The function now respects write permissions and soft-dirty bits when batching PTEs for unmapping, preventing accidental write upgrades and preserving the soft-dirty bit during restoration after a failed unmap.
